title: Diagnostics
description: Every WebFluent error and warning, by code — what it means, a program that draws it, the message the compiler prints, and the fix.

title: A01 — An image with no alt text
description: An `Image` with no `alt`. A screen reader reads the file name; a decorative image takes `alt: ""`.

title: A02 — An icon button with no name
description: An `IconButton` with no `label:`, which is its accessible name.

title: A03 — An input with no label
description: An `Input` with neither `label:` nor `placeholder:`.

title: A04 — A control with no label
description: A `Checkbox`, `Radio`, `Switch`, `Slider` or `Textarea` with no `label:`.

title: A05 — A button with no text
description: A `Button` with no text: no label, no `aria-label:`, and no `Text` in its block.

title: A06 — A link with no text
description: A `Link` with no text.

title: A07 — An empty heading
description: A `Heading` with no text.

title: A08 — A dialog with no title
description: A `Modal`, `Dialog`, `AlertDialog` or `Sheet` with no `title:` (a `Sheet` may take a `label:`), which is its accessible name.

title: A09 — Media nobody can follow without sound
description: A `Video` with no `controls`, or a `Video` or `Audio` with no `captions:` or `transcript:`.

title: A10 — A table with no header row
description: A `Table` with no `Table.Head`.

title: A11 — A skipped heading level
description: A heading level skipped — `h2` straight to `h4`.

title: A12 — A page without exactly one h1
description: A page with no `h1`, or more than one.

title: A13 — Colours without enough contrast
description: A theme's colour pairing falls below the WCAG AA contrast ratio.

title: A14 — A role whose children are the wrong kind
description: A `role:` that requires particular children holds a control that is not one.

title: A15 — An `aria-label` that does not contain the visible text
description: A control's `aria-label` does not contain the text it shows, so what a voice-control user says does not match what they see.

title: A16 — One id on several elements
description: A literal `id:` inside a `for`, or in a component placed more than once, gives several elements one id; a label's `for` and `aria-*` find only the first.

title: A17 — A frame with no title
description: A `Frame` with no `title:`, which is its accessible name: a screen reader announces a frame by its title, and a frame without one as only a frame.

title: A18 — A popover with no name
description: A `Popover` drawn as a dialog (it has no other `role:`) with no `label:`: a screen reader announces it as a dialog and nothing more.

title: C01 — A required prop or field left out
description: A component's prop, or a record's field, that has no default is not given. The value would be `undefined` where the declaration promises one.

title: C02 — A prop the component does not declare
description: Your own component is called with a prop it does not declare. Nothing in it reads the value, so the call does not do what it says; often a misspelling.

title: C03 — A part outside the component it belongs to
description: `Select.Option`, `Table.Row`, `Card.Header` — a part is placed inside its owner. Outside it, it draws a stray element with nothing around it.

title: C04 — An attribute a built-in does not declare
description: A named argument a built-in has no prop for is written to its element as an HTML attribute. `aria-*`, `data-*` and the global attributes are…

title: C05 — A positional argument a built-in does not take
description: The built-in takes its arguments by name; one written without a name is not given to anything.

title: C06 — A positional argument bound by order
description: Your component declares no positional prop (`_ name`), so the argument is bound to its first prop. Mark that prop with `_` to say so.

title: C07 — A drag or a gesture on a component with no one element
description: `drag:`, `dragGroup:`, `dropValue:`, `dropAxis:`, `dropInside:`, `on receive(d)`, `on dragmove(d)`, `on longpress` and `on swipe` written on your…

title: D01 — A file the project does not have
description: A site-relative `src:`, `poster:`, `captions:` or `transcript:` names a file that is not in `public/`; the page asks for it and gets nothing.

title: D02 — A persisted value storage cannot keep
description: `persist` writes its value to the browser's storage as JSON; a function, a file or a promise does not survive it.

title: D03 — A persisted value every instance shares
description: A `persist` in a component placed more than once, or in a loop, is one stored value for all of them. `key:` gives each its own.

title: D04 — A persisted shape changed with no new version
description: What a returning reader's browser holds is the old shape; the page reads it as the new one. Raising `version:`, with a `migrate` step, brings it forward.

title: D05 — An asset from another origin with no integrity hash
description: A stylesheet, font or script loaded from another origin is code that origin can change after you read it. A `meta.integrity` hash is how the browser…

title: D06 — A script loaded on consent, with nothing to ask for it
description: A `meta.scripts` entry marked `"load": "consent"` loads only once the reader accepts in a `ConsentBanner`. With no banner in the program, nobody is…

title: E001 — Text the compiler cannot read
description: A character that begins nothing the language has, or a string, comment or splice that never closes. The file is not read past it.

title: E002 — A syntax error
description: The text reads, but not as the language: a missing brace, a stray word, an argument list that does not close. The message names what was expected and…

title: E003 — Indentation that lines up with no block
description: In a `.wfx` file a line opens a block by being followed by a deeper one, and closes blocks by coming back out. A line that comes back to an…

title: E004 — A file in the WebFluent 2 grammar
description: WebFluent 3 reads one grammar. `wf migrate` rewrites a WebFluent 2 project in place.

title: E005 — A file the formatter will not change
description: `wf fmt` holds its result to the file's tokens; when formatting would change what a file says, it leaves the file alone and says so.

title: E101 — A component nothing declares
description: An element, a `layout:` or a part names a component that no `component` declares and no built-in has. Often a misspelling.

title: E102 — A name declared twice
description: Two declarations with one name in one scope: two stores, two constants, a state and a derived of one name. It compiled to a script the browser…

title: E103 — A flag, case, part, event or slot the component does not have
description: What a component takes comes from one registry for the built-ins and from the declaration for your own; a word that resolves to nothing there does…

title: E104 — A layout with nowhere to put the page
description: A page's `layout:` is a component the page is placed in, at its default slot. A component that declares no `slot` has nowhere to put it.

title: E105 — A statement a render block cannot hold
description: A page's or component's body draws; an assignment or a call that does something belongs in a handler, an `action` or an `effect`.

title: E106 — Script or a whole style in an attribute
description: `onclick:` and the other `on*` attributes are script in a string, which the content security policy refuses and nothing checks. A handler is `on…

title: E107 — A URL a browser would run
description: `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`, `blob:` and `file:` URLs run or load something the page did not write. A link takes `http`, `https`, `mailto`,…

title: E108 — An `env` name that is not public
description: Whatever a page reads from `env` is in the bundle, where anyone can read it. A name a page reads must begin `PUBLIC_` or be listed in `public_env`.

title: E109 — An element this output cannot draw
description: A PDF or a slide deck has no buttons, inputs, handlers or routes; an interactive element in one would be drawn as nothing.

title: E110 — A project script that cannot be a plain script
description: A `.js` file under `src/` is linked as a plain browser script: one with `import` or `export`, one a file in `public/` would replace, or one whose…

title: E111 — A setting that cannot work
description: A value in `webfluent.app.json` that names something that does not exist or asks for something the build cannot do.

title: E112 — A setting nothing reads
description: A key in `webfluent.app.json` that is not a setting. Usually a misspelling, so the setting it meant keeps its default.

title: E113 — An argument that cannot be positional
description: Only the first argument of a call may be written without its name, and only when the component declares a positional prop (`_ name`). Name the others.

title: E114 — `emit` outside a component
description: An event belongs to a component, which declares it and fires it with `emit`; a page has none.

title: E115 — A project script the compiler could not read
description: The file is still linked and may run fine in a browser, but the compiler could not read what it declares, so its names are not in scope for the program.

title: E116 — A tag that cannot be a custom element's
description: `Element` names a custom element by its tag, first and as a string: lower case, with a hyphen (`"stripe-pricing-table"`).

title: E117 — A key combination no keyboard sends
description: `on key(…)` names modifiers (`ctrl`, `shift`, `alt`, `meta`) and one key; a modifier it does not know, no key, or a key no keyboard has would never match.

title: E118 — A name the language already has
description: A name the language gives a meaning cannot be a program's own — not a `state`, `derived`, `persist` or `let`, a prop, a route or action parameter, a…

title: E119 — A hidden direction control in the source
description: An embedding, override or isolate control (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) is invisible and reorders what follows it, so the code a reader sees is not…

title: E120 — Something nests too deeply
description: Brackets, blocks, components that place each other, or the links of one chain (`a.b.c`, `1 + 2 + 3`) nest more than 100 levels deep, which no pass of…

title: E121 — A render that would do too much
description: A template's render would draw more elements and loop items, work out more, or write more markup than one render may: nested loops over vast ranges…

title: E901 — The compiler wrote JavaScript a browser would refuse
description: The build reads back every script it writes, and this one would not run. It is a bug in WebFluent, not in the program; please report it with the…

title: E902 — Output its own security policy refuses
description: The build holds every page to the content security policy it ships beside it — as it wrote the page, and as the page's own `head { }` tags would add…

title: F01 — A `bind:` to something that cannot be written
description: `bind:` writes what the control holds back to what it names: a state, a store's state, or a field of a loop's item. A constant, a derived value, a…

title: F02 — A `bind:` to a state the control cannot hold
description: A text field holds text, a number field (`.number`) a number, a checkbox a `Bool`. Bound to a state of another type, it writes the wrong kind of…

title: F03 — A `validate` block no control can satisfy
description: The rules of a `validate` block are shown on the control bound to the state, and a form is valid when they pass. On a state no control binds, or a…

title: F04 — A checkbox that shows a state and never changes it
description: `Checkbox(checked: x)` with no `bind:` and no `on change` draws `x`, and a click toggles the box while `x` stays as it was.

title: F05 — A select whose value is none of its options
description: The bound state starts as a value no option has, so the select shows its first option while the state holds something else.

title: I01 — A message no translation has
description: `t("key")` names a key no locale's file holds, so the page shows the key itself.

title: I02 — A message and its call that disagree
description: The call passes a value the message does not use, or the message shows a placeholder the call does not pass, which then shows as written.

title: I03 — A message one locale has and another does not
description: A reader in the locale that lacks it sees the default locale's words instead of their own — or, where the default locale is the one that lacks it, the key.

title: I04 — A locale the project does not have
description: `setLocale("xx")` names a locale `i18n.locales` does not list.

title: I05 — Words a reader sees that are not translated
description: Under `i18n.literals`, text that splices more than a name, or a value shown by a name that does not say it is words, is never looked up: every reader…

title: N01 — A path that names no parameter
description: An endpoint's path names its parameters, `at "users/{id}"`: each `{name}` is filled by the parameter of that name. A parameter has one place — the path, a header or a cookie.

title: N02 — A resource over a write
description: A `resource` asks again whenever the page draws it or what it reads changes. A write — `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` — is sent once, from an action or a handler.

title: N03 — A `try` with nowhere to pass its error
description: `try` returns a result's error from the action it is in, so the action must say what it fails with, and that must be able to hold the error.

title: N04 — A result nothing reads
description: A call's result awaited on its own drops whether the call worked. Match it, or pass a failure up with `try`.

title: N05 — An `invalidates` naming what the contract does not have
description: A write's `invalidates [list, byId(id)]` names reads of the same group, each argument one of the write's own parameters. A name the group does not have makes nothing stale.

title: N06 — A `fake` that does not match its group's contract
description: A `fake` answers in place of the network, so it is held to the group's contract: its endpoints, their parameters, and the result each declares.

title: N07 — A service's files are behind its spec
description: A service's files are behind its OpenAPI spec: `wf api sync` would change them, so the program is checked against a contract the server no longer keeps.

title: N08 — A form 7.0 removed
description: `fetch(…)`, an endpoint that does not say how it fails, `errors { }`, and a read's `loading`/`error`/`ready` arms, `.data`, `.state`, `.refreshing` and `on:` were how 6.x asked a service for things and read the answer. In 7.0 a request is `http.get(…)` or an endpoint declared `-> T ! E` or `-> T!`, whose answer is a result, and a read is one value: `.loading`, `.failed(e)` or `.loaded(value)`. Each form has its fix.

title: N09 — A retry asked of a write that is not idempotent
description: A `POST` or `PATCH` whose answer was lost may have been taken, and sent again it would be taken twice — a second order. So it is retried, or replayed offline, only when its endpoint is marked `idempotent`, which sends one `Idempotency-Key` on every try; a `retry:` on any other write does nothing.

title: N11 — `Any` or `Map` where a service meets the program
description: What crosses to a service has a type the program names: a record, a dictionary, or `Json` — never `Any` or `Map`.

title: N12 — An error enum that is not shaped as one
description: An error enum names the statuses a service answers with, each a case with one value, and keeps one `http(error: HttpError)` case for the rest.

title: N14 — A `pages` or `streamed` an endpoint cannot have
description: An endpoint that pages names the parameter the next page goes in and where a page's items are; one that streams answers a list. Each is a read's.

title: P01 — A persisted value with no way forward
description: A `persist` at `version: n` with nothing to bring an older version forward, so what a returning reader had is discarded.

title: P02 — A migration that never runs
description: A `migrate` step above the declared `version:`.

title: P03 — A persisted value in a route-scoped store
description: The route change drops the store, and the next read builds it again from storage, so the value comes straight back.

title: R01 — A route to nothing
description: A link, a `navigate()` or a `Route` names a page or a path that no page has.

title: R02 — A route parameter with no page parameter
description: A route's `:name` fills the page's parameter of that name; a `:name` with no parameter is read as nothing. A parameter with no `:name` is the page's data: the page is a template, which `wf render` and a test hand its data and a build leaves out.

title: R03 — An `app` with no `Router`, or with two
description: The current page is drawn where `app` places its `Router`. With none, no page is ever drawn; with two, the page has two places.

title: R04 — A relative URL on a nested route
description: `"images/x.png"` is fetched relative to the page's address, so on `/blog/post` it is `/blog/images/x.png`. Written from the root, `"/images/x.png"`,…

title: R05 — A translation of no page, or two in one language
description: `translates:` names the page this one is a translation of, and the pages it joins list each other as `hreflang` alternates, each in its own `lang:`.…

title: S01 — A page with no title
description: A page has no `title:`.

title: S02 — A page with no description
description: A page has no `description:`, so its search snippet is written for it.

title: S03 — A description too long for a search result
description: A description longer than about 160 characters, which a search result truncates.

title: S04 — Two pages on one route
description: Two pages claim one path, and only one of them can ever be reached.

title: T01 — A value of the wrong type
description: A value given to a prop, a state, a field, a parameter or an assignment that is not of the type it is declared to hold.

title: T02 — A case the enum does not have
description: `.loud` given where an enum is wanted that has no case `loud`.

title: T04 — A value that may be null, read as if it were not
description: A field or method read from a value that may be `null`. `if let`, `??`, `?.` or a `!= null` check narrows it.

title: T05 — A field or method that does not exist
description: A record, a map literal or a built-in value read for a field or method it does not have.

title: T06 — A member a store or service does not have
description: A store's state, derived value or action, or a service's endpoint, that it does not declare.

title: T07 — A condition that is always true
description: A list, a record or an action used as a condition: it is never `false`, so the branch always runs.

title: T08 — A loop over something that is not a list
description: A `for` over a number, a string or a record.

title: T09 — An `emit` that does not match its event
description: The arguments an `emit` passes are not the ones the event declares.

title: T10 — A call with the wrong arguments
description: Too many or too few arguments, a name the callee does not take, or one of the wrong kind.

title: T11 — A `match` on something that cannot be matched
description: A `match` is over a read, a result, a connection or an enum; its arms are the cases of that kind.

title: T12 — A secret where it would escape
description: A `Secret` shown by an element, spliced into text, logged or kept with `persist`.

title: T13 — A name nothing declares
description: A name, or a function called, that no declaration, parameter, script or browser global provides — a ReferenceError the first time the page reads it.

title: T14 — A comparison that is always the same
description: `==` or `!=` between values that can never be equal — a string and a number, a record and a string, an enum and a case it does not have — so the…

title: T15 — A `match` that misses a case, or has one twice
description: A `match` with no `else` must give every case of the enum an arm — a value with a case it misses would match nothing. A case with two arms reaches…

title: T16 — A method a number, a string or a list does not have
description: In the browser the call is `x.method is not a function`, the first time the line runs. The message suggests the nearest method there is.

title: T17 — An async result used before it is awaited
description: An action that awaits hands back a promise; read as its result without `await` it is not one. `await` is written in an action, a handler, a timer or…

title: T18 — Arithmetic on something that is not a number
description: `-`, `*`, `/` and `%` take numbers; on a string or a list the result is `NaN`. `+` joins two strings or adds two numbers, never one of each: a splice says how a number shows in text.

title: T19 — A value that may be null, shown as text
description: Spliced into text, `null` shows as `null` (and a missing value as `undefined`). Say what to show instead with `??`.

title: T20 — A list or a record shown as text
description: A list in text runs its items together with commas, and a map or a record shows as `[object Object]`. Show a field, or join a list of text.

title: T21 — A read's `match` with no `.failed` arm
description: When the first request fails, a `match` over a read with no `.failed` arm and no `else` shows nothing at all, and the reader is not told.

title: T22 — A handler that names more values than its event sends
description: A handler names the values its event sends, in order: `on menu(key, x, y)` for a component's `event menu(key: String, x: Number, y: Number)`. A DOM…

title: T23 — `Any` written as a type
description: 7.0 took `Any` out of the language: a value of a type nothing checks agreed with every other. Write the type it holds, or `Json` for JSON whose shape is open.

title: T24 — `Map` written as a type
description: 7.0 took `Map` out of the language: it said nothing of its keys or what they hold. Write a `type` with its fields, a dictionary `[String: T]`, or `Json`.

title: T25 — A state whose first value does not say what it holds
description: A `state` or `persist` is inferred only from a value that says everything — a number, a string, a case, a record, a list or map with items. An empty list, an empty map, `null` or open JSON says nothing, so the declaration says what it holds: `state items: [Todo] = []`.

title: T26 — An action that returns a value and does not say what
description: An action that returns a value says what it returns, `-> T`, so a caller in another file reads it without reading the action's body.

title: T27 — Two values with no type in common
description: The branches of an `if` or a `match`, a list's items and the sides of `??` make one value, so they are one type. `null` on one side makes it `T?`.

title: T28 — A `Json` value read as if it were something else
description: `Json` may be an object, a list, a string, a number, a boolean or null. Match its cases, or decode it into a type, before reading it.

title: T29 — A condition that is not a `Bool`
description: `if`, `show`, `!`, `&&` and `||` take a `Bool`. Write the comparison meant: `count != 0`, `name != ""`, `user != null`.

title: T30 — A part of the browser the language does not type
description: A browser global, or a member of an element or an event, the language does not type: reach it from a project script whose JSDoc says its types.

title: T31 — A script's function the language cannot type
description: A project script's JSDoc is its signature. A function called from `.wf` with none, or with a type the language cannot say — a union, an `Array` that does not say what it holds — has no signature to check a call or its result against.

title: T32 — A parameter written with no type
description: What another declaration or a caller sees is declared: an action's, an event's or a slot's parameter says its type, and so does a lambda's when nothing it is passed to says it.

title: T33 — Data that is not what its type says
description: Data from outside the program — a `data` file, a template's data, a test's `data:` — is held to its type where it comes in, and refused with the place it goes wrong.

title: T34 — A conversion the language does not make for you
description: A `Date` or `Time` where text is wanted takes a splice that says how it shows; a `Duration` says its unit, never a bare number.

title: T35 — Values worked out from each other with neither declared
description: Two `derived` values — in one body, or in two stores — that each read the other, or one that reads itself: neither has a type to start from, so one of them must say what it is.

title: U01 — A state nothing reads
description: A `state` nothing in its page or component reads; an assignment alone does not read it.

title: U02 — A derived value nothing reads
description: A `derived` nothing reads.

title: U03 — A component nothing places
description: A component nothing places, names as a layout, or reaches as a part.

title: U04 — A store member nothing reads
description: A store's state, derived value or action that nothing reads, inside the store or as `Store.member`.

title: U05 — An action nothing calls
description: An action nothing calls; a name that starts with `_` is understood to be unused on purpose.

title: U06 — Code after return
description: What follows a `return` in the same block never runs.

title: U07 — An allow that allows nothing
description: A `// wf-allow(CODE)` comment covers the next line of code (or its own, at the end of one); when nothing it names is reported there, or it names an…

title: U08 — A condition that is always the same
description: A literal condition, or a value compared with itself, decides the same way every time; one branch never runs.

title: U09 — An unkeyed loop whose items hold state

title: wf init
description: Create a new WebFluent project

title: wf inspect
description: One page as a reader meets it, as text: landmarks, headings, links, buttons, fields, tables, and anything that failed

title: wf migrate
description: Carry a project forward: WebFluent 2 → 3, 3 → 4, 4 → 4.2 and 6 → 7, each step that applies

title: wf motion
description: The animations an element can play, the eases and speeds, the route transitions and the project's default

title: wf registry
description: Describe every built-in component: props, cases, flags, events, slots, parts

title: wf render
description: Render a .wf template with JSON data

title: wf rules
description: The rules a `validate` block may hold, the named patterns, when a form shows its messages, and every state the project holds to a rule

title: wf scope
description: What a path picker lists at a place: the names in scope there, each with its type and where it comes from, and the fields to go on into

title: wf serve
description: Start the development server

title: wf start
description: Serve a built project as a host would: `$PORT`, the build's headers and compressed files, a single-page build's shell for every route, and `--proxy` for an API elsewhere

title: wf test
description: Run the project's `test "…" { … }` declarations under tests/

title: wf theme
description: The theme the build uses: every token, declared or inherited, where each is used, and its contrast pairs

title: wf translations
description: The translations as a table: each locale's plural forms and what it lacks, each key's messages, and where a `t()` names it

title: wf types
description: Describe what a project declares: enums, types, components, stores, pages

title: wf verify
description: Load every page of a built project in a real browser: errors, failed requests, paint timing, and which built-ins it drew

title: ClientOnly
description: Its block drawn in the browser alone, never in the static paint, a template or a PDF: a clock, the reader's own data. A placeholder { … } block is what those show in its place.

title: Code
description: Inline code, or a code block with block; language: colours it.

title: CodeBlock
description: A block of code with a bar above it: a file name, a copy button (.copy), and line numbers (.lines). language: colours it, as on Code; highlight: marks lines; files: makes it a tab for each file.

title: CodeBlock.Bar
description: The bar above the code.

title: CodeBlock.Lines
description: The line numbers.

title: CodeBlock.Mark
description: One line's mark. Drawn for it.

title: CodeBlock.Marks
description: The marks over the lines highlight: names. Drawn for it.

title: ColorPicker
description: A colour, chosen from swatches: (each a button, the chosen one pressed), with the browser's own picker, or typed as hex; bind: holds it as #rrggbb.

title: Column
description: A child of the 12-column grid, spanning span columns.

title: Combobox
description: A text field that offers what matches as the reader types: from options:, or search: asked of a server. The arrow keys go through the offers, Enter takes one, Escape closes them; .multiple keeps several, each a chip Backspace takes back. option(o) { … } draws an offer; empty { … } shows when nothing matches.

title: CommandPalette
description: A dialog of everything a reader can do or go to, filtered as they type: the arrow keys go through what matches, Enter runs it (on select) and closes. open: is the state that shows it.

title: CommandPalette.Group
description: Items under a heading.

title: CommandPalette.Item
description: One thing to do or go to; on select is what it does.

title: CommandPalette.List
description: What matches. Drawn for it.

title: Configuration
description: Every key of webfluent.app.json, its type and default: project, build, media, PDF, slides, dev, motion, meta, theme, i18n, env, offline and lints.

title: ConsentBanner
description: The reader's say over the scripts that track them: shown until they choose, Decline as easy as Accept, and the choice kept. Accepting loads the meta.scripts entries marked "load": "consent", then and on every later visit; nothing loads before.

title: ConsentSettings
description: A button that asks the reader again — a footer's "Cookie settings": it forgets their answer and shows the ConsentBanner. A script already loaded stays until the page is loaded again.

title: Container
description: Centred wrapper with a maximum width and horizontal padding.

title: ContextMenu
description: What it wraps, and a menu a right-click, a long press, the menu key or Shift+F10 inside it opens where it happened.

title: ContextMenu.Items
description: The menu: Menu.Items, Menu.Subs and Menu.Dividers.

title: CopyButton
description: A button that copies value: to the clipboard, says Copied for a moment, and tells a screen reader so.

title: DataTable
description: Rows of records with their columns declared once: a column sorts when it is .sortable (its header a button, aria-sort saying which way), cell(r) { … } draws a cell, empty { … } shows when there are no rows, and bind: chooses rows (a list with .multiple, a box for each and one for all).

title: DataTable.Column
description: One column: its title, its value: (what it shows and sorts by), and a cell(r) { … } that draws it instead.

title: DatePicker
description: A date field: the reader picks a day, and the bound state holds a Date.

title: DateRangePicker
description: A first and a last day, chosen in two months side by side that a button opens, or by a preset: presets: [.last7, .thisMonth]. bind: holds { start, end }.

title: DescriptionList
description: Terms and what they are (<dl>): a column of pairs, or .grid, each term beside its value.

title: DescriptionList.Details
description: A value. Drawn for it.

title: DescriptionList.Item
description: One pair: its term, and value: or its block.

title: DescriptionList.Term
description: A term. Drawn for it.

title: Dialog
description: Confirmation <dialog>, opened by a state flag. on close runs when it closes, however it was closed, and the focus goes back to what had it.

title: Dialog.Title
description: What the dialog's heading draws, in place of its title:'s words, which stay its name.

title: Divider
description: Horizontal rule.

title: Document
description: Root of a PDF document: the paper, the margins and what the file says about itself.

title: Dropdown
description: Button that opens a menu of Dropdown.Items.

title: Dropdown.Divider
description: A rule between groups of entries.

title: Dropdown.Item
description: One entry of the menu.

title: Editable
description: Text that turns into a field when pressed: Enter or leaving keeps what was typed, Escape puts it back; bind: holds the text.

title: Editors
description: Editor support for WebFluent: what wf-lsp answers, what the VS Code and Zed extensions and the Tree-sitter grammars support, and how to install each.

title: Element
description: A custom element a script defines, placed by its tag: Element("stripe-pricing-table", publishableKey: key) { on ready { … } }. Every named argument is an attribute, every on handler an event it fires, and the block its children.

title: EmptyState
description: What a list or a page shows when it has nothing yet: an icon, a title, a sentence and, in its block, what to do about it.

title: EmptyState.Actions
description: What to do: the block it was given.

title: EmptyState.Text
description: Its sentence.

title: EmptyState.Title
description: Its title.

title: Expressions
description: Literals, interpolation and formatted splices, operators and precedence, if and match as values, lambdas, methods, format and ago, regexes, tokens, await.

title: Fab
description: A round button floating at the bottom of the screen for the page's main action; with Fab.Actions in its block it opens them instead (a speed dial).

title: Fab.Action
description: One more action the button opens: its words and its icon; on click is what it does.

title: Fab.Trigger
description: Its button. Drawn for it.

title: Field
description: A label, a hint and an error around a control of your own: the first control in its block is named by the label and described by the hint and the error, and marked invalid while there is one.

title: Field.Error
description: Its error, announced as it appears. Drawn for it.

title: Field.Hint
description: Its hint. Drawn for it.

title: Field.Label
description: Its label. Drawn for it.

title: Fieldset
description: Controls that belong together — an address, a choice of plan — under a legend that names them.

title: Fieldset.Legend
description: Its legend. Drawn for it.

title: FileUpload
description: File input; bind: holds what was chosen, and on change hears it.

title: Footer
description: Repeated at the bottom of every PDF page (or those on: names), where page and pages are the page's number and the count; a <footer> on the web.

title: Form
description: Groups controls; on submit runs when it is submitted, and the page never navigates away.

title: Frame
description: Another page, shown inside this one: an iframe — the page at src:, or the HTML srcdoc: gives it, sandboxed as sandbox: says. on message(m) hears what that page posts to this one (m.data), and nothing any other page posts. Without title: it draws an A17 warning: a frame is announced by its title.

title: Gallery
description: Pictures in a grid of columns: (unset, as many as fit), each cropped to one shape — ratio:, unset square. In a Lightbox, each opens full screen.

title: Glossary
description: The terms this guide uses — state, signal, pre-rendered page, hydration, flag, part, slot, registry, scope and more — each in a sentence, with a link.

title: Grammar
description: The WebFluent grammar on one page: keywords, declarations, render and imperative blocks, components, tests, styles, operators, precedence and literals.

title: Grid
description: CSS grid with a fixed number of columns.

title: Header
description: Repeated at the top of every PDF page (or those on: names), where page and pages are the page's number and the count; a <header> on the web.

title: Heading
description: Heading; level picks the tag (h2 when none is given).

title: Highlight
description: Text with every match of query: marked (<mark>), as a search's results show what was found; the case is ignored.

title: Host
description: A bare node handed to somebody else's code, with a lifetime. mount: runs with the node each time it is made, update: again whenever the state it reads changes, and cleanup: when the page, branch or list item it belongs to leaves. Every other element takes the same three.

title: HoverCard
description: A preview card at a link or a button: shown after delay: ms of hover, at once on focus; it stays while the pointer is on it, and goes when the pointer leaves both, on Escape or on a press outside.

title: HoverCard.Content
description: What the card shows. The rest of the block is what it is at.

title: Icon
description: One of the built-in SVG icons, rendered inline.

title: IconButton
description: Icon-only button. label is its accessible name, never visible text.

title: Image
description: Image; alt is required for accessibility (rule A01). Given an image the program declares, it becomes a <picture> with every width the build wrote.

title: ImageSlide
description: Image slide with an optional caption.

title: Input
description: Text field. With label, hint or error it is a labelled field.

title: InputGroup
description: An input drawn as one box with what goes beside it: an icon, InputGroup.Addon("https://"), a button, or InputGroup.Clear, which empties the input and gives it the focus back.

title: InputGroup.Addon
description: Text beside the input: https://, .com, kg.

title: InputGroup.Clear
description: A button that empties the input and puts the focus back in it; hidden while it is empty.

title: InputOTP
description: A one-time code typed a digit to a box: the focus moves on as each is typed and back with Backspace, and a code pasted into any box fills them all; the browser offers the code it was sent (autocomplete="one-time-code").

title: Item
description: A row of a list, a settings page or a search's results: Item.Media at its start, its title: and description:, then its block, and Item.Actions at its end.

title: Item.Actions
description: What goes at its end: a switch, a button, a menu.

title: Item.Content
description: Its title, description and block. Drawn for it.

title: Item.Media
description: What goes at its start: an icon, an avatar, a picture.

title: Kbd
description: A key or a combination, written as this system writes it: Kbd("mod+k") is ⌘K on a Mac and Ctrl+K elsewhere.

title: Library
description: The compiler as a library: the webfluent crate (Template, build, memory, vfs, diagnostics, config, errors, semver), the Node package and wf.js.

title: Lightbox
description: Every picture in its block opens, on a press or Enter, full screen: the arrow keys and a swipe go between them, a double press or + zooms, Escape closes and the focus goes back. A picture's data-full: is the file it opens, else its largest size.

title: Link
description: Client-side navigation link; its label or its block is the link text.

title: List
description: List of its children; ordered for a numbered list.

title: List.Item
description: One entry (<li>).

title: Listbox
description: A list of options always shown, one chosen (selection follows the arrow keys) or, .multiple, several: Space chooses, Shift with an arrow takes the next one in too, Ctrl or ⌘ with A takes them all; a letter goes to the next option that starts with it.

title: Listbox.Option
description: One option: its words, and the value bind: holds when it is chosen.

title: LoadingOverlay
description: A region covered while it is busy: aria-busy on it, its content out of reach, and a spinner with label: over it — the region, not the page.

title: LoadingOverlay.Content
description: The region. Drawn for it.

title: LoadingOverlay.Cover
description: What covers it while it is busy. Drawn for it.

title: LocaleSwitch
description: One button for each of i18n.locales, each written in its own language (English, العربية), the current one pressed; a press is setLocale.

title: Markdown
description: Markdown text rendered as HTML: headings, paragraphs, lists, quotes, code, links, emphasis. The text is escaped first, so HTML in it is shown, not run, and a link or picture whose URL a browser would run is drawn as its words. .inert is for text somebody else wrote.

title: Masonry
description: Its children in columns: columns, each placed under the last in its column, keeping its own height.

title: Menu
description: A menu above everything: opened by its trigger: button, or by visible: at an anchor: or a point at: — a context menu. Escape, a press outside or a choice close it, write false back to visible: and fire on close.

title: Menu.Divider
description: A rule between groups of entries.

title: Menu.Item
description: One entry of the menu; on click is what choosing it does.

title: Menu.Sub
description: An entry that opens a menu of its own beside it.

title: Menubar
description: File, Edit and View, as in a desktop app: one Tab stop, the arrow keys along it; Down or Enter opens a menu, and with one open Left and Right open the one beside it.

title: Menubar.Menu
description: One menu of the bar: its button's words, and its Menu.Items, Menu.Subs and Menu.Dividers.

title: Meter
description: A level against its range (<meter>): a disk's use, a password's strength. Past high: or under low: it says so in its colour; optimum: says which end is good.

title: Modal
description: Modal <dialog>, opened by a state flag; the browser supplies focus trapping and Escape. on close runs when it closes, however it was closed, and the focus goes back to what had it.

title: Modal.Footer
description: The modal's action row.

title: Modal.Title
description: What the modal's heading draws, in place of its title:'s words, which stay its name: Modal.Title { Text { "Rename "  Code(name) } }.

title: Navbar
description: Top navigation bar with brand, links and action areas.

title: Navbar.Actions
description: Buttons at the end of the bar.

title: Navbar.Brand
description: The brand area, usually a link home.

title: Navbar.Links
description: The navigation links; collapses behind a toggle on small screens.

title: NavigationMenu
description: A site's main navigation whose entries open panels (a mega menu) as disclosures: one open at a time, the arrow keys along the row, Down into a panel, Escape, a press outside or the focus leaving closes it.

title: NavigationMenu.Item
description: An entry that opens a panel: its words are its button, its block the panel.

title: NavigationMenu.Link
description: An entry that is a link, beside the ones that open panels.

title: NavigationMenu.List
description: Its entries. Drawn for it.

title: NavigationMenu.Panel
description: An entry's panel. Drawn for it.

title: NavigationMenu.Trigger
description: An entry's button. Drawn for it.

title: NumberInput
description: A number with − and + beside it: the arrow keys step it, PageUp and PageDown by ten steps, and it stays between min: and max:.

title: NumberInput.Decrease
description: Its − button. Drawn for it.

title: NumberInput.Increase
description: Its + button. Drawn for it.

title: OnThisPage
description: The page's headings as links, the one being read marked as the reader scrolls: a table of contents beside a long page.

title: OnThisPage.Title
description: Its title. Drawn for it.

title: Option
description: One choice in a Select (the original spelling of Select.Option).

title: PageBreak
description: Forces a new PDF page.

title: Pagination
description: Pages of a list: Previous, the first and last pages, those around the current one with a gap for the rest, and Next. The current page is aria-current="page"; bind: holds it, from 1.

title: Pagination.Gap
description: The pages left out. Drawn for it.

title: Pagination.Next
description: The next page. Drawn for it.

title: Pagination.Page
description: A page. Drawn for it.

title: Pagination.Prev
description: The previous page. Drawn for it.

title: PanelGroup
description: Panels side by side (or .vertical, one above another) with a handle between each two that resizes them: dragged, or the arrow keys on it. bind: holds their sizes in percent — a persist keeps them across visits — and on resize(e) hears them as e.detail.

title: PanelGroup.Panel
description: One panel.

title: Paragraph
description: Block of text with paragraph spacing.

title: Popconfirm
description: A question beside the button in its block before what it does: the button opens it, on confirm hears yes, on cancel no or Escape; the focus starts on the answer that loses nothing.

title: Popover
description: A layer at a control: drawn above everything, placed against its anchor:, closed by Escape or a press outside, which write false back to visible: and fire on close.

title: Portal
description: Its block, drawn into a node somebody else's code owns: an element a script hands over, or a ref: handle. When into: names another node the block moves there with its nodes and state; null keeps it aside until a node comes back; it goes when the page, branch or list item it is written in leaves. What is inside belongs to where it is written: its handlers, emit and lifetimes.

title: Presentation
description: Root of a slide deck; its children must be slides.

title: PrevNext
description: The pages before and after this one in an ordered set — a guide's chapters: each a link that says which way it goes and the page's title.

title: PrevNext.Next
description: The page after: its title, and where it is.

title: PrevNext.Prev
description: The page before: its title, and where it is.

title: Progress
description: Progress bar; a value that reads state moves with it.

title: Project structure
description: Where files go, how they merge into one program, naming in a global namespace, wf generate, what to commit, and how to grow a project.

title: QrCode
description: A QR code for a URL or any text, drawn as vector graphics when the page is built.

title: Radio
description: One choice of a group; every radio bound to the same state is one group.

title: RadioGroup
description: One choice of several, as native radio buttons under a legend: the arrow keys move between them, and .cards draws each as a card with its hint.

title: RadioGroup.Hint
description: An option's hint. Drawn for it.

title: RadioGroup.Legend
description: Its legend. Drawn for it.

title: RadioGroup.Option
description: One choice: its words, its value, and a hint said with it.

title: Rating
description: Stars, as radio buttons a screen reader hears as a choice of one to max:: the arrow keys move between them; .half takes halves; .readonly only shows.

title: RelativeTime
description: A moment as 3 minutes ago, kept current, with the exact time on hover (<time>).

title: Services and requests
description: Lookup tables for api, endpoints, http calls and resources: settings, options, members, HttpError, caching, retry, middleware, fakes and codes.

title: Route
description: Maps a path to a page (the original grammar; pages now declare their paths).

title: Router
description: Where the current page renders. May sit at any depth inside app; pages declare their own paths.

title: Row
description: Horizontal flex layout. It stays a row at every width unless .stacks or a responsive direction says otherwise.

title: Runtime API
description: The runtime reference, window.WF: signals, elements, motion, routing, data and results, stores, widgets, safety, text and boot, module by module.

title: ScrollArea
description: A box that scrolls within height:, with a thin scrollbar, its edges fading where there is more, and a Tab stop so a keyboard can scroll it.

title: Section
description: Groups content with spacing; on the web, a <section>.

title: SectionSlide
description: Full-bleed coloured band with a centred label.

title: Select
description: Drop-down of Select.Option children.

title: Select.Option
description: One choice: the visible label, and the value sent with the form.

title: Sheet
description: A modal <dialog> that comes in from an edge: the bottom (a phone's filters, a share list) or the start or end of the line. Dragged by its handle or heading toward its edge it closes; a bottom sheet with snap: points settles at the nearest.

title: Sheet.Footer
description: The sheet's action row, kept in view below what scrolls.

title: Sheet.Title
description: What the sheet's heading draws, in place of its title:'s words, which stay its name.

title: Sidebar
description: Side navigation. A Sidebar.Item whose to matches the current route is marked .active and aria-current="page".

title: Sidebar.Divider
description: A rule between groups of items.

title: Sidebar.Header
description: The sidebar's heading area.

title: Sidebar.Item
description: One navigation entry.

title: Skeleton
description: Placeholder shape shown while content loads.

title: Slide
description: One slide, one PDF page; content is top-aligned and clipped at the bottom margin.

title: Slider
description: Range input. aria-* and its other attributes reach the input; with aria-valuetext the raw number is not shown beside the track.

title: Spacer
description: Vertical space; md when no size is given.

title: Sparkline
description: A tiny chart in a line of text — a line, or .bar — of a list of numbers, drawn as an SVG when the page is built.

title: Spinner
description: Loading indicator, announced as a status.

title: Splitter
description: A handle that sets the size of a region beside it: dragged, between min: and max:; double-clicked or Enter, back to reset:; the arrow keys move it.

title: Stack
description: Vertical flex layout.

title: Stat
description: A figure with its label — revenue, sign-ups — and how it moved: Stat("Revenue", value: total, format: .currency, change: 0.124). count: counts to a new value.

title: Stat.Change
description: How it moved, with its direction.

title: Stat.Label
description: Its label.

title: Stat.Value
description: Its figure.

title: Stepper
description: Steps taken in order — an account, then billing, then a summary — with each step's state (done, current, an error) and the current step's block shown. bind: holds the current step, from 0; .linear keeps a step out of reach until the ones before it are passed.

title: Stepper.Item
description: A step in the list. Drawn for it.

title: Stepper.List
description: The steps, in order. Drawn for it.

title: Stepper.Step
description: One step: its title in the list, its block shown while it is the current one.

title: Sticky
description: A box that sticks to the top of its scrolling parent (offset: below it) as the page scrolls past, marked data-stuck while it is stuck.

title: Switch
description: On/off toggle bound to a boolean state.

title: Table
description: Data table. Cells inside Table.Head render as <th scope="col">; caption is the table's accessible name, visually hidden.

title: Table.Body
description: The body of a table: its rows of data.

title: Table.Cell
description: A cell. header makes it a <th> anywhere, as Table.Head does for its cells.

title: Table.Head
description: Header section; its cells become <th scope="col">.

title: Table.Row
description: A row of cells.

title: TableOfContents
description: The document's headings with the page each lands on, each a link to it.

title: TabPage
description: One tab inside Tabs (the original spelling of Tabs.Page).

title: Tabs
description: Tab strip switching between its pages: the arrow keys move between the tabs (the other way round in a right-to-left page), Home and End go to the ends.

title: Tabs.Page
description: One tab and its panel.

title: Tag
description: Compact chip.

title: TagInput
description: Words typed into a field, each a chip once Enter or a comma ends it; Backspace in the empty field takes the last back, and each chip has a button to take it out.

title: Tbody
description: Table body section (the original spelling of Table.Body).

title: Tcell
description: Table cell (the original spelling of Table.Cell).

title: Text
description: A paragraph of text. {…} in the string reads state and stays live.

title: Textarea
description: Several lines of text. With label, hint or error it is a labelled field; with maxLength it counts what is left.

title: Thead
description: Table header section (the original spelling of Table.Head).

title: ThemeToggle
description: A button that switches the page between light and dark, over setTheme: a moon in a light page, a sun in a dark one, named for the theme it switches to. The reader's choice is kept.

title: Timeline
description: Events in order (<ol>), each a dot on a line, its title, its time and its block.

title: Timeline.Item
description: One event: its title, at: its time, and its block.

title: Timeline.Time
description: An event's time (<time>). Drawn for it.

title: TitleSlide
description: Cover slide: title and subtitle, vertically centred.

title: Toast
description: Temporary notification.

title: Toggle
description: A button that stays pressed while its state holds — bold in an editor, a filter that is on: aria-pressed, a press flipping bind:.

title: ToggleGroup
description: Buttons of which one is chosen — a view switcher, a segmented control — or, .multiple, several: one stop for Tab, the arrow keys inside it, each aria-pressed. bind: holds the chosen value: (a list with .multiple).

title: ToggleGroup.Item
description: One choice: its words, and the value bind: holds when it is chosen.

title: Design tokens
description: Every baseline design token: its default value, what it is for, which built-ins draw from it, and how a style block or a stylesheet reads it.

title: Tooltip
description: Shows text above everything when its child is hovered (after delay:) or focused from the keyboard.

title: Tour
description: A tour of the page while open: holds: each step in a card at its target: (a ref:), lit through a cut-out in the dimmed page, with Back, Next and Done; Escape ends it and writes false back. on finish hears Done, on close any end.

title: Tour.Step
description: One step: what it points at, its title, and its block.

title: TransferList
description: Two lists side by side — what can be chosen and what is — with buttons that move the selected across, or all of them; bind: holds the keys of the chosen.

title: Tree
description: Nested items — files and folders, an outline — as a tree a keyboard can work: Up and Down through what shows, Right to open and go in, Left to close and go out (the other way round right to left), Home and End, a letter. row(item) { … } draws each; bind: holds the chosen item's key, or a list of keys with .multiple.

title: Trow
description: Table row (the original spelling of Table.Row).

title: TwoColumn
description: Two equal columns; takes exactly two Container children.

title: Unsafe
description: The one door for markup a page did not write. It has a single part, Unsafe.Html.

title: Unsafe.Html
description: Markup, put in as markup. It is **not** sanitised — the name says so — and sanitize(…) is one call away for anything the project did not write itself.

title: Video
description: Video player. Without captions it draws an A09 warning: a video nobody can hear is a video nobody can follow.

title: VirtualList
description: A scrolling box that draws only the rows in view of the one keyed for inside it — for a tree, search results or a diff of thousands of rows.

title: VisuallyHidden
description: Words for a screen reader only: Link(…) { Text("Docs")  VisuallyHidden("(opens in a new tab)") }.

title: Watermark
description: Large, faint, rotated text behind each PDF page's content.

title: Showcase
description: Sites, documents and decks made with WebFluent.
